endpoint.description: The base URL endpoint for connecting to the Timeplus Enterprise. When it's not set, `http://localhost:8000` will be used.

block.description:
The Timeplus provider is used to interact with the resources supported by [Timeplus Enterprise](https://www.timeplus.com/). The provider needs to be configured with an username and password before it can be used.

Use the navigation to the left to read about the available resources.

description.description: A detailed text describes the dashboard

id.description: The dashboard immutable ID, generated by Timeplus

name.description: The human-friendly name for the dashboard

panels.description: A list of panels defined in a JSON array. The best way to generate such array is to copy it directly from the Timeplus console UI.

block.description: A dashboard is a set of one or more panels organized and arranged in one web page. A variety of panels are supported to make it easy to construct the visualization components so that you can create the dashboards for specific monitoring and analytics needs.

description.description: A detailed text describes the javascript function

is_aggregate_function.description: Indecates if the javascript function an aggregate function

return_type.description: The type of the function's return value

block.description: Describe an argument of the javascript function, argument order matters

Timeplus javascript functions are one of the supported user defined function types. Javascript functions allow users to implement functions with the javascript programming language, and be called in queries.

description.description: A detailed text describes the view

history_ttl.description: A SQL expression defines the maximum age of historical data

query.description: The query SQL of the view. Changing the SQL will lead to a recreation.

retention_bytes.description: The retention size threadhold in bytes indicates how many data could be kept in the streaming store

retention_ms.description: The retention period threadhold in millisecond indicates how long data could be kept in the streaming store

target_stream.description: The optional stream name that the materialized view writes data to

block.description: Timeplus materialized views are special views that persist its data. Once created, a materialized view will keep running in the background and continuously writes the query results to the underlying storage system.

auth_header.description: The HTTP header and its value to be used as an authentication means to call the function. The remote function can use this information to determine if it's a valid call

description.description: A detailed text describes the remote function

return_type.description: The type of the function's return value

url.description: The HTTP endpoint to be used to call the function

block.description: Describe an argument of the remote function, argument order matters
Timeplus remote functions are one of the supported user defined function types. Remote functions allow users to register a HTTP webhook as a function which can be called in queries.

description.description: A detailed text describes the sink

id.description: The sink immutable ID, generated by Timeplus

name.description: The human-friendly name for the sink

properties.description: A JSON object defines the configurations for the specific sink type. The properites could contain sensitive information like password, secret, etc.

query.description: The query the sink uses to generate data

type.description: The type of the sink, refer to the Timeplus document for supported sink types

block.description: Timeplus sinks run queries in background and send query results to the target system continuously.

description.description: A detailed text describes the source

id.description: The source immutable ID, generated by Timeplus

name.description: The human-friendly name for the source

properties.description: A JSON object defines the configurations for the specific source type. The properites could contain sensitive information like password, secret, etc.

stream.description: The target stream the source ingests data to

type.description: The type of the source, refer to the Timeplus document for supported source types

block.description: Timeplus sources are processes run in background to collect data from specific data sources and ingest them into streams.

description.description: A detailed text describes the stream

history_ttl.description: A SQL expression defines the maximum age of data that are persisted in the historical store

mode.description: The stream mode. Options: append, changelog, changelog_kv, versioned_kv. Default: "append"

retention_bytes.description: The retention size threadhold in bytes indicates how many data could be kept in the streaming store

retention_ms.description: The retention period threadhold in millisecond indicates how long data could be kept in the streaming store

default.description: The default value for the column

primary_key.description: If set to `true`, this column will be used as the primary key, or part of the combined primary key if multiple columns are marked as primary keys.

type.description: The type name of the column

use_as_event_time.description: If set to `true`, this column will be used as the event time column (by default ingest time will be used as event time). Only one column can be marked as the event time column in a stream.

block.description: Define the columns of the stream

Timeplus streams are similar to tables in the traditional SQL databases. Both of them are essentially datasets. The key difference is that Timeplus stream is an append-only (by default), unbounded, constantly changing events group.

description.description: A detailed text describes the view

query.description: The query SQL of the view

block.description: Timeplus views are named queries. When you create a view, you basically create a query and assign a name to the query. Therefore, a view is useful for wrapping a commonly used complex query.
